conditions.name: Migraine
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Study migraine recognition, acute treatment, and secondary-headache warning signs.

sources.title: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Management of Headache – Provider Summary
sources.organization: US Department of Veterans Affairs / Department of Defense

sources.title: Tension Headaches, Migraine, and More
sources.organization: National Institutes of Health

sections.title: Clinical pattern
sections.text: Recurrent migraine attacks can combine severe headache, nausea, and light or sound sensitivity; unilateral pain is common but not universal.

sections.title: Acute treatment
sections.text: VA/DoD recommends specified triptans, including sumatriptan, for an acute migraine attack; selection requires checking contraindications.

sections.title: Secondary headache warnings
sections.text: Thunderclap onset, focal neurologic findings, fever, papilledema, or major pattern change require assessment for secondary causes.

questions.stem: A 34-year-old has recurring 8-hour one-sided headaches with nausea and marked light sensitivity. Episodes interrupt work. Which diagnosis best fits?
questions.explanation: The headache with nausea and sensory sensitivity supports migraine.

distractorExplanations.A: Usually milder and bilateral.
distractorExplanations.B: This lacks the typical cluster pattern.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize the migraine symptom pattern.

questions.stem: A nonpregnant adult with established migraine has an attack despite simple analgesia. Cardiovascular and other triptan contraindications are excluded. Which listed acute option is guideline-supported?
questions.explanation: Sumatriptan is an acute migraine option in Recommendation 19.

distractorExplanations.A: Not an acute migraine option.
distractorExplanations.D: No infection is described.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish acute migraine therapy from unrelated drugs.

conditions.name: Tension-type headache
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Study the tension-type pattern, chronic prevention, and headache reassessment.

sources.title: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Management of Headache – Provider Summary
sources.organization: US Department of Veterans Affairs / Department of Defense
sources.locator: Recommendation 25; Sidebar 1; Sidebar 3, Common Primary Headache Disorders Criteria (printed pages 7–8; PDF page indexes 10–11)

sources.title: Tension Headaches, Migraine, and More
sources.organization: National Institutes of Health

sections.title: Clinical pattern
sections.text: Tension-type headaches often feel like bilateral pressure, remain mild to moderate, and do not worsen with routine activity. Nausea and vomiting are absent; stress and poor sleep may contribute.

sections.title: Chronic prevention
sections.text: VA/DoD suggests amitriptyline for chronic tension-type headache prevention, after considering adverse effects and individual risks.

sections.title: Reassessment
sections.text: Review headache frequency and medication use. New abrupt severe pain or neurologic changes should prompt secondary-headache evaluation.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old describes recurrent three-hour mild bilateral pressing headaches after stressful shifts and poor sleep. Walking or climbing stairs does not worsen the pain. There is no nausea, vomiting, aura, or light or sound sensitivity. Which primary headache pattern is most likely?
questions.explanation: Bilateral pressing pain without activity aggravation or nausea favors tension-type headache.

distractorExplanations.A: Severe clustered attacks are not described.
distractorExplanations.B: Aura and typical migraine-associated features are absent.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize a likely tension-type presentation.

questions.stem: An adult with confirmed chronic tension-type headache seeks preventive medication. Which listed drug is suggested by VA/DoD?
questions.explanation: Recommendation 25 suggests amitriptyline for chronic tension-type prevention.

distractorExplanations.A: Not headache prevention.
distractorExplanations.D: Not the guideline's suggested TTH preventive.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a supported chronic tension-type preventive.

conditions.name: Acute ischemic stroke
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Study emergency recognition and the bounded 2026 acute reperfusion recommendation.

sources.title: Top Things to Know: 2026 Guideline for the Early Management of Patients With AIS
sources.organization: American Heart Association / American Stroke Association

sources.title: Signs and Symptoms of Stroke
sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.locator: Signs and symptoms; When to seek emergency help

sections.title: Emergency recognition
sections.text: Sudden unilateral weakness or speech difficulty warrants emergency stroke evaluation; record symptom onset and activate emergency transport.

sections.title: Disabling deficit and reperfusion
sections.text: For eligible disabling ischemic stroke within 4.5 hours, the 2026 guideline supports alteplase or tenecteplase; eligibility remains essential.

sections.title: Disability matters
sections.text: A low NIHSS score alone does not exclude thrombolysis when deficits are disabling. Non-disabling deficits follow a different treatment pathway.

questions.stem: In clinic, a 68-year-old suddenly develops right arm weakness and aphasia. Symptoms began 20 minutes ago. What is the best next action?
questions.explanation: Acute focal deficits require immediate emergency stroke evaluation.

distractorExplanations.A: Delays time-sensitive evaluation.
distractorExplanations.D: Does not address the acute event.

questions.learningObjective: Prioritize emergency evaluation of acute focal deficits.

questions.stem: A stroke team confirms ischemic stroke with disabling aphasia 90 minutes after onset. Hemorrhage and all thrombolysis contraindications are excluded. Which statement matches the 2026 guideline?

choices.text: NIHSS must exceed a fixed cutoff
Either alteplase or tenecteplase is supported

questions.explanation: Eligible disabling stroke supports rapid IV thrombolysis with either agent.

distractorExplanations.A: Both agents are endorsed.
distractorExplanations.D: Treatment should be prompt.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the 2026 early thrombolysis recommendation.

conditions.name: Transient ischemic attack
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Study urgent assessment after resolved deficits and appropriate brain imaging.

sources.title: Top Things to Know: Diagnosis, Workup, Risk Reduction of Transient Ischemic Attack in the Emergency Department Setting
sources.organization: American Heart Association

sources.title: Signs and Symptoms of Stroke
sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.locator: What should I do to treat a transient ischemic attack?

sections.title: Resolved symptoms remain important
sections.text: Resolution of a focal deficit does not remove the need for prompt assessment; suspected TIA signals serious stroke risk.

sections.title: Brain imaging
sections.text: The AHA statement prefers MRI with diffusion-weighted imaging for tissue assessment; CT plus CTA offers a practical alternative when needed.

sections.title: Risk assessment and follow-up
sections.text: Disposition combines neurologic evaluation and vessel imaging with risk assessment. Early neurology input is preferable to a score alone.

questions.stem: A 71-year-old had sudden unilateral weakness and speech difficulty that resolved before arrival. Which response is most appropriate?

choices.text: Treat only if symptoms persist a week

questions.explanation: Resolved focal symptoms still warrant prompt suspected-TIA evaluation.

distractorExplanations.A: Resolution does not remove stroke risk.
distractorExplanations.D: Persistence is not required.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize urgency despite symptom resolution.

questions.stem: During a suspected-TIA workup, MRI is immediately available and there is no contraindication. Which test best assesses small ischemic brain tissue lesions?
questions.explanation: The AHA statement prefers MRI-DWI for brain tissue assessment.

distractorExplanations.D: Does not identify ischemic tissue.

questions.learningObjective: Choose sensitive tissue imaging in suspected TIA.

conditions.name: Epilepsy
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: US federal recommendation/reference module on ongoing self-management and seizure first aid. A current comprehensive US pharmacologic epilepsy guideline was not verified; the 2015 AAN first-seizure guideline is excluded pending currency confirmation.

sources.title: Epilepsy
sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus

sources.title: First Aid for Seizures
sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.locator: How to keep someone safe during a seizure; When to call for help; What to avoid

sources.title: Managing Epilepsy
sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
sources.locator: Everyday strategies: Understand epilepsy and your treatment; Manage your seizures

sections.title: Aim for seizure control
sections.text: Medication can control seizures for many people. Persistent seizures warrant reassessment; selected patients may need other treatment approaches.

sections.title: Provide safe first aid
sections.text: Protect from nearby hazards, position safely and time the seizure. A seizure lasting more than five minutes requires emergency help; do not restrain or put objects in the mouth.

sections.title: Support adherence and tracking
sections.text: Take antiseizure medicine as prescribed, discuss other drugs and supplements with the clinician, and track seizures and potential triggers.

questions.stem: An adult has an ongoing generalized convulsive seizure that has lasted six minutes. The area is cleared and the person is positioned safely. What additional action is indicated?

choices.text: Force a spoon into the mouth
Wait an hour before seeking help

questions.explanation: CDC advises emergency help when a seizure lasts longer than five minutes.

distractorExplanations.A: Objects in the mouth can injure.
distractorExplanations.D: Food or water can cause choking.
distractorExplanations.E: The duration already meets the emergency criterion.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize the seizure first-aid emergency threshold

questions.stem: A patient with established epilepsy frequently forgets prescribed medication and has difficulty describing breakthrough events. Which plan best supports ongoing management?

choices.text: Stop medication whenever symptoms seem absent
Improve prescribed-dose adherence and keep a seizure record
Take medicine only after a seizure

questions.explanation: CDC supports taking medication as prescribed and tracking seizures.

distractorExplanations.A: Feeling well does not justify self-discontinuation.
distractorExplanations.B: Supplements should be discussed with the clinician.
distractorExplanations.D: This is not prescribed maintenance use.

questions.learningObjective: Use adherence and tracking in epilepsy self-management

conditions.name: Benign paroxysmal positional vertigo
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Reference-only US federal module. A formal US BPPV guideline is not incorporated because AAO-HNS app/AI reuse restrictions need resolution; no substitute guideline is claimed.

sources.title: Balance Disorders
sources.organization: National Institute on Deafness and Other Communication Disorders
sources.locator: What are some types of balance disorders?; How are balance disorders treated?; How can I help my doctor make a diagnosis?

sections.title: Recognize the positional pattern
sections.text: BPPV produces brief spinning episodes with specific head-position changes. Displaced inner-ear particles disturb vestibular signals.

sections.title: Characterize dizziness carefully
sections.text: Record episode duration, positional triggers, associated hearing symptoms, falls and medicines. Dizziness has multiple possible causes and may warrant specialist assessment.

sections.title: Know the treatment mechanism
sections.text: A trained clinician may use an Epley maneuver to relocate displaced particles in BPPV. Some people need more than one treatment session.

questions.stem: An adult has brief spinning when rolling over in bed, with no symptoms between episodes. Which listed disorder best fits this pattern?
questions.explanation: Brief vertigo triggered by a head-position change fits the described BPPV pattern.

distractorExplanations.B: Anxiety alone does not specifically explain this positional pattern.
distractorExplanations.C: Insomnia does not explain the vertigo.
distractorExplanations.D: A wrist neuropathy does not explain this pattern.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize a typical BPPV history

questions.stem: A clinician confirms BPPV in a patient suitable for a repositioning maneuver. Which listed intervention addresses the displaced inner-ear particles?

choices.text: Chronic diazepam as a particle-removing drug
Daily aspirin as a particle-removing drug

questions.explanation: The Epley maneuver can relocate particles contributing to BPPV.

distractorExplanations.B: Antibiotics do not mechanically relocate particles.
distractorExplanations.C: Diazepam does not remove the particles.
distractorExplanations.D: Steroids do not mechanically relocate particles.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a particle-repositioning intervention

conditions.name: Alzheimer dementia
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Diagnostic evaluation of suspected Alzheimer disease and related dementias in primary care; this module does not cover all biomarker or disease-modifying treatment eligibility.

sources.title: Alzheimer's Association clinical practice guideline for the Diagnostic Evaluation, Testing, Counseling, and Disclosure of Suspected Alzheimer's Disease and Related Disorders (DETeCD-ADRD): Executive summary of recommendations for primary care
sources.organization: Alzheimer's Association

sections.title: Do not dismiss symptoms
sections.text: Investigate reported cognitive change. Obtain both the patient's account and collateral information about cognition and everyday function.

sections.title: Assess contributing conditions
sections.text: The initial evaluation includes a focused examination, laboratory assessment and structural brain imaging; MRI is preferred when available and appropriate.

sections.title: Include the care partner
sections.text: Assess understanding and decision-making capacity, then communicate the evaluation and care plan with the patient and an appropriate care partner.

questions.stem: A 73-year-old reports increasing memory difficulty. Her daughter describes missed bills over eight months. What best strengthens the initial assessment?

choices.text: Obtain patient and informant histories of cognition and function
Diagnose Alzheimer disease solely from age
Skip assessment because she lives independently
Use a blood biomarker as the entire evaluation

questions.explanation: Collateral functional history is part of the recommended diagnostic assessment.

distractorExplanations.A: Symptoms warrant evaluation.
distractorExplanations.D: Living independently does not exclude impairment.
distractorExplanations.E: A biomarker does not replace the clinical evaluation.

questions.learningObjective: Use collateral history in cognitive evaluation

questions.stem: A patient undergoing an initial dementia evaluation can safely undergo MRI, and MRI is available. Which structural study is preferred?
questions.explanation: MRI is the preferred structural imaging modality in this setting.

distractorExplanations.A: Skull films do not assess brain structure.
distractorExplanations.B: Auscultation is not structural brain imaging.
distractorExplanations.C: Cervical films do not evaluate dementia.
distractorExplanations.D: Structural imaging is part of the evaluation.

questions.learningObjective: Select structural imaging for suspected dementia

conditions.name: Delirium
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Recognition and cause-directed care, with formal US guidance specifically for postoperative delirium in older adults; this is not a complete ICU delirium protocol.

sources.title: Delirium
sources.organization: National Library of Medicine, MedlinePlus
sources.edition: Current web reference; publication date not stated
sources.locator: What are the symptoms of delirium?; What are the treatments for delirium?

sources.title: American Geriatrics Society Abstracted Clinical Practice Guideline for Postoperative Delirium in Older Adults
sources.organization: American Geriatrics Society
sources.locator: Sections II, IV, XIII and XIV

sections.title: Acute fluctuating attention
sections.text: Abrupt confusion with impaired attention and changing alertness suggests delirium. A person with dementia can also develop delirium.

sections.title: Identify contributors
sections.text: Evaluate and address underlying illness, medication effects and other contributors. Support orientation, sensory aids, hydration and sleep.

sections.title: Avoid routine sedation
sections.text: For postoperative delirium without threatening agitation, do not routinely give antipsychotics or benzodiazepines. Withdrawal syndromes require a different assessment.

questions.stem: An older inpatient was conversant yesterday but now cannot sustain attention. Alertness varies over hours. What best characterizes this change?

choices.text: A normal response requiring no assessment

questions.explanation: Acute, fluctuating impairment of attention is characteristic of delirium.

distractorExplanations.A: Normal aging does not explain this abrupt change.
distractorExplanations.C: Slow progression alone does not explain hourly fluctuation.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize delirium from its time course and attention deficit

questions.stem: After surgery, an older adult has quiet delirium without aggression or dangerous behavior. Alcohol and sedative withdrawal are excluded. Which approach is best?

choices.text: Scheduled haloperidol for every delirium case
Investigate causes and provide supportive care

questions.explanation: Cause-directed evaluation and supportive care are appropriate; routine sedating drugs are discouraged here.

distractorExplanations.A: Antipsychotics are not routine treatment in this scenario.
distractorExplanations.D: Delirium needs prompt assessment.
distractorExplanations.E: Routine restraint is not the recommended approach.

questions.learningObjective: Manage non-dangerous postoperative delirium

conditions.name: Major depressive disorder
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Treatment selection and continuation after a confirmed adult MDD diagnosis; acute suicidality, psychosis, catatonia and possible bipolar illness require separate assessment.

sources.title: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Major Depressive Disorder: Provider Summary
sources.organization: Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense

sections.title: Select initial treatment
sections.text: For uncomplicated MDD, psychotherapy or antidepressant monotherapy can be selected with patient preference. SSRIs are among supported initial medications.

sections.title: Measure response
sections.text: Track symptoms with a quantitative measure during care. Severe, persistent or recurrent depression may warrant combined psychotherapy and medication.

sections.title: Protect remission
sections.text: After remission with an antidepressant, continue the effective therapeutic regimen for at least six months to reduce relapse risk.

questions.stem: An adult with confirmed uncomplicated MDD prefers medication. There is no mania history, psychosis or acute safety concern. Which class is supported for initial treatment?

choices.text: MAOI as the routine first choice
Ketamine as the routine first choice

questions.explanation: An SSRI is among guideline-supported initial antidepressant choices.

distractorExplanations.A: MAOIs are discouraged as initial therapy.
distractorExplanations.B: Ketamine is not routine initial treatment.
distractorExplanations.E: Routine antipsychotic monotherapy is not the recommendation.

questions.learningObjective: Choose an initial antidepressant class

questions.stem: A patient has reached remission from a first uncomplicated depressive episode on a well-tolerated antidepressant. What continuation plan best matches the guideline?

choices.text: Continue the effective regimen for at least six months
Stop on the first symptom-free day
Take it only on difficult days
Stop after one week of remission

questions.explanation: Continuation for at least six months after remission reduces relapse risk.

distractorExplanations.C: A benzodiazepine is not a replacement antidepressant.
distractorExplanations.D: Intermittent use is not the recommended regimen.
distractorExplanations.E: One week is shorter than the recommended continuation.

questions.learningObjective: Plan antidepressant continuation after remission

conditions.name: Generalized anxiety disorder
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Reference-only module based on the US NIMH publication revised in 2025. A comprehensive current US formal GAD guideline was not verified; this is not presented as complete guideline coverage.

sources.title: Generalized Anxiety Disorder: What You Need to Know
sources.organization: National Institute of Mental Health

sections.title: Persistent difficult-to-control worry
sections.text: GAD involves difficult-to-control worry on most days for at least six months, with associated symptoms and clinically important impact.

sections.title: Offer evidence-based psychotherapy
sections.text: CBT is an established psychotherapy for GAD. Treatment selection depends on the person's needs, preferences and medical situation.

sections.title: Discuss medication tradeoffs
sections.text: SSRIs and SNRIs can treat GAD but take weeks to work. Benzodiazepines can cause tolerance and dependence and may be prescribed only briefly.

questions.stem: An adult has diagnosed GAD with substantial functional impairment and prefers psychotherapy. Which option has specific support in the NIMH reference?

choices.text: Avoidance of all feared activities as the sole intervention

questions.explanation: CBT is supported by the NIMH treatment reference.

distractorExplanations.A: Reassurance alone is inadequate for the stated impairment.
distractorExplanations.B: Surgery is not a GAD treatment.
distractorExplanations.D: Alcohol is not a recommended treatment.
distractorExplanations.E: Avoidance alone is not evidence-based CBT.

questions.learningObjective: Choose an evidence-based psychological treatment

questions.stem: A patient with GAD requests indefinite daily diazepam because it acts quickly. What concern best explains why this is unsuitable as routine long-term care?

choices.text: They require years before any effect
They cure every anxiety disorder permanently
They are the only effective GAD treatment
They can produce tolerance and dependence

questions.explanation: Tolerance and dependence limit routine long-term benzodiazepine use.

distractorExplanations.A: The drug class is not antibacterial.
distractorExplanations.B: They act rapidly rather than after years.
distractorExplanations.D: Other established treatments exist.

questions.learningObjective: Counsel about long-term benzodiazepine limitations

conditions.name: Bipolar disorder
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Selected adult treatment decisions after bipolar disorder is established; acute dangerous mania and pregnancy-related prescribing need separate assessment.

sources.title: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Management of Bipolar Disorder: Provider Summary
sources.organization: Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense

sections.title: Match therapy to episode polarity
sections.text: Lithium or quetiapine are suggested for acute mania. Suspected mania during antidepressant treatment warrants a clinical reassessment.

sections.title: Treat bipolar depression specifically
sections.text: Quetiapine monotherapy has a strong recommendation for acute bipolar depression. A unipolar depression treatment plan should not be assumed equivalent.

sections.title: Plan relapse prevention
sections.text: Maintenance choices depend on the episode pattern. Lamotrigine has strong support for preventing recurrence of bipolar depressive episodes.

questions.stem: A nonpregnant adult with established bipolar disorder has an acute depressive episode without imminent danger. Which listed monotherapy has strong VA/DoD support for this episode?
questions.explanation: Quetiapine is strongly recommended for acute bipolar depression.

distractorExplanations.B: Donepezil is not the recommended mood treatment.
distractorExplanations.C: Diazepam does not constitute recommended episode treatment.
distractorExplanations.D: Methotrexate is not a bipolar medication.

questions.learningObjective: Choose therapy for acute bipolar depression

questions.stem: A patient with bipolar disorder needs a maintenance plan focused on preventing recurrent depressive episodes. Which listed agent has strong guideline support for that purpose?
questions.explanation: Lamotrigine is recommended for prevention of bipolar depressive recurrence.

distractorExplanations.A: Diphenhydramine is not maintenance mood therapy.
distractorExplanations.B: An antibiotic does not prevent mood episodes.
distractorExplanations.E: Clopidogrel is not a mood stabilizer.

questions.learningObjective: Select maintenance treatment by episode polarity

conditions.name: Post-traumatic stress disorder
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Selected adult PTSD treatment and response-monitoring recommendations; this module does not reproduce copyrighted therapy manuals or diagnostic scales.

sources.title: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Management of Posttraumatic Stress Disorder and Acute Stress Disorder: Provider Summary
sources.organization: Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense

sections.title: Prioritize trauma-focused therapy
sections.text: Recommended individual therapies include prolonged exposure, cognitive processing therapy and EMDR. The guideline favors recommended psychotherapy over medication when feasible.

sections.title: Measure change
sections.text: Use a validated PTSD severity instrument, such as PCL-5, to track response while continuing a clinical assessment.

sections.title: Avoid benzodiazepines for PTSD
sections.text: The guideline recommends against benzodiazepines as PTSD treatment. A sedative response does not establish effective treatment of core symptoms.

questions.stem: An adult with established PTSD is willing and able to engage in structured psychotherapy. Which listed treatment is specifically recommended?

choices.text: Supportive conversation as the only intervention for every patient
Avoiding any discussion of trauma indefinitely

questions.explanation: Prolonged exposure is a recommended individual PTSD psychotherapy.

distractorExplanations.C: This does not provide the specified evidence-based intervention.
distractorExplanations.D: Sleep deprivation is not recommended.
distractorExplanations.E: Avoidance is not the recommended therapeutic approach.

questions.learningObjective: Identify a recommended trauma-focused psychotherapy

questions.stem: A patient requests chronic clonazepam to treat core PTSD symptoms. Which response best matches the VA/DoD guideline?

choices.text: Explain that benzodiazepines are recommended against for PTSD treatment
Recommend it for all patients with PTSD
Use it instead of every trauma-focused therapy
Prescribe it indefinitely because sedation proves recovery

questions.explanation: The guideline specifically recommends against benzodiazepines for PTSD.

distractorExplanations.B: The guideline recommends against this use.
distractorExplanations.C: It should not replace recommended therapy.
distractorExplanations.D: Escalation does not address the guideline concern.
distractorExplanations.E: Sedation does not demonstrate PTSD recovery.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the PTSD benzodiazepine recommendation

conditions.name: Alcohol use disorder
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Treatment selection for moderate or severe AUD, separate from medically managed alcohol withdrawal.

sources.title: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Substance Use Disorders: Provider Summary
sources.organization: Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense
sources.locator: Recommendations 5, 12 and 15; medication contraindication table, printed page 18

sections.title: Offer ongoing treatment
sections.text: Naltrexone and topiramate have strong guideline support for moderate or severe AUD; combine treatment planning with an appropriate psychosocial intervention.

sections.title: Check opioid exposure
sections.text: Naltrexone is contraindicated with current opioid agonist treatment or physiological opioid dependence. Assess opioid use before selecting it.

sections.title: Separate withdrawal care
sections.text: Moderate or severe alcohol withdrawal requires monitored treatment; benzodiazepines are recommended in that setting, distinct from long-term AUD medication.

questions.stem: An adult with moderate AUD requests medication. There is no opioid use, withdrawal, acute hepatitis or severe hepatic impairment. Which listed medication has strong guideline support?
questions.explanation: Naltrexone is a strongly supported AUD medication when contraindications are absent.

distractorExplanations.A: An antibiotic does not treat AUD.
distractorExplanations.D: Donepezil is not an AUD therapy.
distractorExplanations.E: Amlodipine is not an AUD therapy.

questions.learningObjective: Select a supported AUD medication

questions.stem: A patient taking methadone for OUD also seeks AUD treatment. Which consideration specifically rules out initiating naltrexone now?
questions.explanation: Current opioid agonist treatment is a contraindication to naltrexone.

distractorExplanations.A: Age alone is not this contraindication.
distractorExplanations.C: Counseling is compatible with AUD care.
distractorExplanations.E: A normal liver test does not create this contraindication.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize a naltrexone contraindication

conditions.name: Opioid use disorder
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Evidence-based ongoing OUD treatment; this module does not provide induction dosing or substitute for overdose emergency care.

sources.title: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Substance Use Disorders: Provider Summary
sources.organization: Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense

sources.title: Opioid Use Disorder: Treating
sources.organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

sections.title: Treat beyond withdrawal
sections.text: Withdrawal management alone is discouraged because relapse and overdose risk remain. Offer ongoing medication treatment and additional support.

sections.title: Know the treatment medications
sections.text: Buprenorphine, methadone and naltrexone are OUD treatment medications. Choice depends on individual needs, opioid exposure and treatment setting.

sections.title: Distinguish rescue from maintenance
sections.text: Naloxone reverses opioid overdose; it is not a substitute for maintenance OUD treatment. Overdose education and access are important parts of care.

questions.stem: An adult with OUD completes withdrawal management and asks how to reduce relapse risk. Which plan is best supported?

choices.text: Provide no ongoing treatment after withdrawal
Offer detoxification again whenever relapse occurs as the sole plan
Use naloxone alone as daily maintenance
Offer ongoing OUD medication treatment with appropriate support

questions.explanation: Ongoing medication treatment addresses risks that withdrawal-only care leaves untreated.

distractorExplanations.A: Withdrawal alone leaves substantial risk.
distractorExplanations.D: Disulfiram is not an OUD treatment medication.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish OUD maintenance from detoxification

questions.stem: A patient asks which listed medicine treats OUD rather than only reversing an overdose. Which is correct?
questions.explanation: Buprenorphine is an OUD treatment medication; naloxone is an overdose antidote.

distractorExplanations.A: Naloxone is rescue treatment.
distractorExplanations.C: Acamprosate is not an OUD medication.
distractorExplanations.D: Disulfiram is not an OUD medication.

questions.learningObjective: Identify medication treatment for OUD

conditions.name: Chronic insomnia disorder
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Adult chronic insomnia treatment after evaluation of contributing conditions; behavioral protocols may need adaptation for specific comorbidities.

sources.title: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Chronic Insomnia Disorder and Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Provider Summary
sources.organization: Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense

sections.title: Use CBT-I first
sections.text: CBT-I is recommended and preferred initially, addressing sleep behaviors and sleep-related thinking.

sections.title: Hygiene is an adjunct
sections.text: Sleep hygiene supports care but is discouraged as the sole chronic-insomnia treatment.

sections.title: Choose medication carefully
sections.text: When medication is appropriate, doxepin is suggested; benzodiazepines, diphenhydramine and trazodone are discouraged.

questions.stem: An adult has insomnia three nights weekly for four months with daytime impairment. Assessment identifies no untreated sleep apnea, unstable mood illness or substance-use concern. Which initial treatment is preferred?
questions.explanation: CBT-I is preferred initially for chronic insomnia.

distractorExplanations.A: Education alone is discouraged as sole treatment.
distractorExplanations.C: Alcohol is not a recommended therapy.
distractorExplanations.D: Benzodiazepines are discouraged.

questions.learningObjective: Choose initial treatment for chronic insomnia

questions.stem: After adequate CBT-I, a clinician and adult patient decide a short medication course is appropriate. Contraindications and interactions are excluded. Which listed option is suggested by VA/DoD?
questions.explanation: Doxepin is suggested when medication is appropriate.

distractorExplanations.D: Benzodiazepines are discouraged.

questions.learningObjective: Distinguish supported from discouraged insomnia medications

conditions.name: Obstructive sleep apnea
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Adult OSA testing and first-line treatment principles; test selection depends on cardiopulmonary and other comorbidities.

sources.title: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Management of Chronic Insomnia Disorder and Obstructive Sleep Apnea: Provider Summary
sources.organization: Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense

sources.title: Sleep Apnea Treatment
sources.organization: National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute
sources.locator: Positive airway pressure devices; healthy lifestyle changes

sections.title: Confirm with objective testing
sections.text: Use a sleep study to diagnose OSA. Home testing suits selected patients; advanced heart failure favors laboratory polysomnography.

sections.title: Do not accept a failed home study
sections.text: If OSA remains suspected after a negative, inconclusive or inadequate home study, perform further sleep testing.

sections.title: Keep the airway open
sections.text: PAP treats OSA; CPAP pressure keeps the airway open. Weight management and lifestyle changes remain adjuncts when indicated.

questions.stem: An adult with suspected OSA also has advanced heart failure. Which diagnostic approach is preferred under the VA/DoD testing guidance?

choices.text: No testing if snoring is loud
A normal daytime oxygen reading as exclusion

questions.explanation: Advanced heart failure favors laboratory polysomnography.

distractorExplanations.A: A questionnaire is not diagnostic.
distractorExplanations.D: CT is not the recommended sleep test.
distractorExplanations.E: Daytime oxygen does not rule out OSA.

questions.learningObjective: Choose sleep testing in complicated suspected OSA

questions.stem: A patient beginning CPAP for confirmed OSA asks how it works. Which explanation is most accurate?

choices.text: It delivers pressure that helps keep the airway open
It cures OSA by suppressing all breathing effort
It substitutes for every weight-management intervention

questions.explanation: CPAP provides continuous pressure to maintain airway patency during sleep.

distractorExplanations.A: CPAP is not surgery.
distractorExplanations.D: It does not aim to suppress breathing.

questions.learningObjective: Explain the mechanism of CPAP

conditions.name: Acute low back pain
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Initial adult assessment and imaging decisions, emphasizing the distinction between uncomplicated pain and neurologic emergencies.

sources.title: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Diagnosis and Treatment of Low Back Pain: Provider Summary
sources.organization: Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense

sections.title: Look for serious features
sections.text: Assess neurologic findings and red flags for serious causes. New urinary retention or saddle sensory loss raises concern for cauda equina syndrome.

sections.title: Avoid unnecessary initial imaging
sections.text: For acute low back pain without focal neurologic deficits or red flags, routine imaging is recommended against.

sections.title: Escalate suspected compression
sections.text: Suspected cauda equina syndrome requires emergent imaging, with MRI preferred when feasible. This is a different pathway from uncomplicated mechanical pain.

questions.stem: An adult has two days of back pain after lifting. Examination is neurologically normal, with no trauma, cancer history, fever, weight loss or bowel/bladder symptoms. Which imaging plan is appropriate initially?

choices.text: Urgent MRI for every lifting injury

questions.explanation: Routine imaging is discouraged when neurologic deficits and red flags are absent.

distractorExplanations.A: The scenario lacks indications for urgent MRI.
distractorExplanations.C: A bone scan is not routinely indicated.
distractorExplanations.E: Serial radiographs are not the initial plan.

questions.learningObjective: Avoid unnecessary imaging in uncomplicated acute back pain

questions.stem: A patient with back pain develops new urinary retention and saddle sensory loss. MRI is available and not contraindicated. What is the appropriate imaging response?

choices.text: Reassure because urinary symptoms exclude a spinal cause
Defer evaluation until weakness becomes permanent

questions.explanation: These findings raise concern for cauda equina syndrome and require emergent imaging.

distractorExplanations.C: Plain films do not adequately evaluate this concern.
distractorExplanations.D: These are concerning spinal red flags.
distractorExplanations.E: Permanent deficit should not be awaited.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize the imaging urgency of suspected cauda equina syndrome

conditions.name: Osteoarthritis
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Hip and knee OA care using the June 2026 VA/DoD guideline, with September 2026 ACR update context; hand OA and all procedural choices are outside this module.

sources.title: VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for the Non-Surgical Management of Hip and Knee Osteoarthritis: Provider Summary
sources.organization: Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense

sources.title: American College of Rheumatology Updates Osteoarthritis Guidance, Reinforcing Personalized, Comprehensive Care
sources.organization: American College of Rheumatology
sources.locator: Core treatment recommendations; new conditional recommendations

sections.title: Build an active care plan
sections.text: Physical activity and individualized exercise are central. For knee OA with overweight or obesity, weight loss is strongly recommended by VA/DoD.

sections.title: Consider topical treatment
sections.text: Topical NSAIDs are suggested for knee OA. Medication selection still requires individual contraindication and interaction assessment.

sections.title: Use the current recommendation scope
sections.text: VA/DoD discourages initiating opioids, including tramadol. The September 2026 ACR update retains core exercise and weight management while adding selected conditional options.

questions.stem: A patient with symptomatic knee OA and obesity asks which non-drug measure should be part of care. Which is strongly recommended by VA/DoD?
questions.explanation: Weight loss is strongly recommended for knee OA with overweight or obesity.

distractorExplanations.A: Bed rest is not the recommended strategy.

questions.learningObjective: Apply weight-management guidance to knee OA

questions.stem: An adult with localized knee OA seeks medication. Contraindications to NSAIDs are excluded. Which listed option is suggested by VA/DoD?
questions.explanation: Topical NSAIDs are a suggested knee OA treatment.

distractorExplanations.A: Initiating opioids is discouraged.
distractorExplanations.B: Amoxicillin is not an OA therapy.
distractorExplanations.C: Donepezil is not an OA therapy.
distractorExplanations.E: Disulfiram is not an OA therapy.

questions.learningObjective: Select a supported medication option for knee OA

conditions.name: Osteoporosis
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Pharmacologic treatment principles for postmenopausal osteoporosis; this guideline scope does not encompass every age, sex or secondary cause.

sources.title: Pharmacological Management of Osteoporosis in Postmenopausal Women Guideline Resources
sources.organization: Endocrine Society

sections.title: Treat high fracture risk
sections.text: Postmenopausal women at high fracture risk, especially after a recent fracture, warrant pharmacologic treatment in addition to bone-health measures.

sections.title: Use appropriate initial therapy
sections.text: Bisphosphonates are recommended initial options for high-risk postmenopausal osteoporosis. Reassess risk before considering a bisphosphonate holiday.

sections.title: Do not stop denosumab casually
sections.text: Do not delay or stop denosumab without subsequent therapy to address rebound bone loss and fracture risk. Bisphosphonate holiday rules do not transfer to denosumab.

questions.stem: A postmenopausal woman has a recent fragility fracture and high fracture risk. Renal function, swallowing ability and other contraindications permit an oral bisphosphonate. Which listed initial medication is recommended?
questions.explanation: Alendronate is a bisphosphonate option for high-risk postmenopausal osteoporosis.

distractorExplanations.A: This is not osteoporosis treatment.
distractorExplanations.D: This is not osteoporosis treatment.

questions.learningObjective: Choose initial osteoporosis pharmacotherapy

questions.stem: A woman receiving denosumab asks to skip future injections as a drug holiday. Which plan best addresses the guideline warning?

choices.text: Wait for a fracture before reassessing
Apply the same holiday schedule as every bisphosphonate
Arrange a planned subsequent antiresorptive strategy before discontinuation

questions.explanation: Subsequent therapy is needed to address rebound risk when denosumab is stopped.

distractorExplanations.A: Unplanned discontinuation creates rebound risk.
distractorExplanations.D: An antibiotic is not a substitute.

questions.learningObjective: Avoid an unprotected denosumab interruption

conditions.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Selected adult RA treatment decisions under the 2021 ACR guideline, still listed on the official RA guideline index; individual comorbidities alter prescribing.

sources.title: 2021 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Treatment of Rheumatoid Arthritis
sources.organization: American College of Rheumatology
sources.locator: DMARD-naive moderate-to-high disease activity; glucocorticoids; treat-to-target recommendations

sections.title: Begin disease-modifying treatment
sections.text: For DMARD-naive moderate-to-high activity RA, methotrexate monotherapy is strongly preferred over several alternative initial monotherapies when appropriate.

sections.title: Adjust toward a target
sections.text: Treat-to-target includes monitoring disease activity and adjusting DMARD treatment toward low activity or remission, rather than addressing pain alone.

sections.title: Limit glucocorticoids
sections.text: Longer-term glucocorticoids are strongly discouraged as routine accompaniment to DMARD initiation. If needed, minimize dose and duration.

questions.stem: A nonpregnant adult has newly confirmed moderate-to-high activity RA and has never taken a DMARD. Relevant methotrexate contraindications are excluded. Which initial monotherapy is strongly preferred?
questions.explanation: Methotrexate is strongly preferred for this initial moderate-to-high activity scenario.

distractorExplanations.A: Hydroxychloroquine has a different role, including some low-activity cases.
distractorExplanations.B: It is not preferred over methotrexate here.
distractorExplanations.D: A biologic is not the preferred initial monotherapy here.
distractorExplanations.E: A JAK inhibitor is not preferred initial monotherapy here.

questions.learningObjective: Choose initial DMARD therapy by RA activity

questions.stem: A patient on optimized methotrexate remains above the agreed RA disease-activity target. Which principle should guide the next step?

choices.text: Treat pain alone and never measure activity
Reassess activity and adjust the DMARD strategy toward the target
Replace all DMARDs with indefinite prednisone
Stop monitoring once any improvement occurs
Wait for irreversible deformity before changing therapy

questions.explanation: Treat-to-target links activity assessment with treatment adjustment.

distractorExplanations.A: Pain-only care omits disease control.
distractorExplanations.C: Indefinite steroid substitution is not the strategy.
distractorExplanations.D: Improvement may still fall short of the target.

questions.learningObjective: Apply treat-to-target RA management

conditions.name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Adult CTS diagnosis and counseling using the 2024 AAOS guideline; the copyrighted CTS-6 instrument itself is not reproduced.

sources.title: Management of Carpal Tunnel Syndrome: Evidence-Based Clinical Practice Guideline
sources.organization: American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
sources.locator: Summary recommendations, printed pages 6–7; diagnosis and corticosteroid-injection chapters

sections.title: Use a structured clinical assessment
sections.text: AAOS supports CTS-6 clinical assessment in place of routine ultrasound or electrodiagnostic testing for diagnosis in appropriate adult presentations.

sections.title: Avoid routine MRI for diagnosis
sections.text: AAOS recommends against MRI as a diagnostic test for CTS. Choose testing to resolve the actual clinical question.

sections.title: Counsel about long-term outcomes
sections.text: Corticosteroid injection has not demonstrated long-term improvement of CTS in the guideline evidence; it should not be presented as a reliably lasting cure.

questions.stem: An adult has a typical suspected CTS presentation. Which listed diagnostic approach does AAOS support as an alternative to routine ultrasound or electrodiagnostic testing?
questions.explanation: AAOS supports CTS-6 clinical assessment for this purpose.

distractorExplanations.A: Brain CT does not answer this question.
distractorExplanations.B: Lumbar puncture is not the CTS assessment.
distractorExplanations.C: MRI is recommended against for CTS diagnosis.
distractorExplanations.E: An ankle index evaluates another system.

questions.learningObjective: Select a supported CTS diagnostic approach

questions.stem: A patient with CTS asks whether one corticosteroid injection is a reliably lasting cure. Which counseling statement matches the guideline?

choices.text: Long-term improvement has not been demonstrated
It eliminates all need for reassessment
It is proven to regenerate every injured nerve
It is equivalent to permanent surgical release in every case

questions.explanation: The evidence does not demonstrate long-term improvement from corticosteroid injection.

distractorExplanations.A: A universal cure claim is unsupported.
distractorExplanations.D: Nerve regeneration is not the demonstrated result.

questions.learningObjective: Counsel about the limits of CTS injection

conditions.name: Acne vulgaris
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Selected treatment principles from the 2024 AAD recommendations; isotretinoin requires its separate prescribing and reproductive-safety requirements.

sources.title: American Academy of Dermatology issues updated guidelines for the management of acne
sources.organization: American Academy of Dermatology
sources.locator: Strong recommendations; good practice statements; severe acne

sections.title: Combine useful mechanisms
sections.text: Benzoyl peroxide and topical retinoids are strongly supported. Regimens can combine complementary topical mechanisms.

sections.title: Protect antibiotic effectiveness
sections.text: Use benzoyl peroxide with topical or oral antibiotics to reduce resistance risk. Limit systemic antibiotic exposure when feasible.

sections.title: Recognize treatment failure
sections.text: Isotretinoin is recommended for severe acne or acne that has failed standard oral or topical therapy, subject to its separate safety requirements.

questions.stem: An adult is starting doxycycline for inflammatory acne. Which topical addition specifically follows the AAD good-practice statement for limiting antibiotic resistance?

choices.text: Petroleum jelly as the sole resistance strategy

questions.explanation: Benzoyl peroxide accompanies acne antibiotics to reduce resistance risk.

distractorExplanations.A: Petroleum jelly does not provide this resistance strategy.
distractorExplanations.D: Ketoconazole is not the recommended addition.
distractorExplanations.E: Lidocaine does not provide this resistance strategy.

questions.learningObjective: Combine acne antibiotics with benzoyl peroxide

questions.stem: A nonpregnant adult has severe scarring acne despite adequate standard topical treatment and an oral antibiotic course. What medication warrants consideration with the required safety program?
questions.explanation: Isotretinoin is recommended for severe or treatment-refractory acne.

distractorExplanations.A: Indefinite ineffective antibiotics are not the recommended escalation.
distractorExplanations.B: Lifelong antibiotic treatment is not the recommended escalation.
distractorExplanations.D: Donepezil is not acne therapy.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize acne warranting isotretinoin consideration

conditions.name: Atopic dermatitis
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Topical care and systemic-steroid cautions, including the 2025 adult focused update and first AAD pediatric guideline issued April 2026; agent-specific age approvals are not inferred.

sources.title: Atopic dermatitis clinical guideline
sources.organization: American Academy of Dermatology
sources.edition: 2023 adult topical guideline; 2025 focused update; current official guideline highlights
sources.locator: Adult topical therapy; focused update; treatment-resistant disease

sources.title: American Academy of Dermatology issues first pediatric atopic dermatitis guidelines
sources.organization: American Academy of Dermatology
sources.locator: Moisturizers and topical treatments; systemic corticosteroids

sections.title: Support the barrier and control inflammation
sections.text: Moisturizers and topical anti-inflammatory treatment are supported. Choose topical corticosteroid potency and site appropriately rather than applying one regimen everywhere.

sections.title: Reassess before escalating
sections.text: Persistent disease despite treatment warrants reassessment of diagnosis, exposures and adherence. The adult focused update adds selected newer therapies.

sections.title: Apply pediatric guidance deliberately
sections.text: The 2026 pediatric recommendations support moisturizers and appropriate topical treatments and recommend against routine systemic corticosteroids. Check individual drug age indications separately.

questions.stem: An adult has a localized, noninfected atopic dermatitis flare on the forearm. Which initial plan best reflects supported topical care?

choices.text: Daily oral antibiotics despite no infection
Chronic oral prednisone for every localized flare
Moisturizer plus an appropriate topical corticosteroid

questions.explanation: Barrier care and appropriate topical anti-inflammatory treatment are supported.

distractorExplanations.A: No infection indication is present.
distractorExplanations.C: Routine systemic steroids are not the topical approach.
distractorExplanations.D: Acyclovir does not treat uncomplicated eczema.

questions.learningObjective: Select initial topical care for eczema

questions.stem: A child with atopic dermatitis is proposed indefinite oral prednisone as routine maintenance. Which response matches the 2026 AAD pediatric guidance?

choices.text: Approve indefinite prednisone for every child
Assume every adult drug is approved at every pediatric age
Treat every flare with an antibiotic
Use the recommended topical strategy and avoid routine systemic corticosteroids

questions.explanation: Routine systemic corticosteroids are recommended against in pediatric AD.

distractorExplanations.A: This conflicts with the recommendation.
distractorExplanations.D: Antibiotics are not routine for noninfected eczema.

questions.learningObjective: Apply the pediatric systemic-corticosteroid caution

conditions.name: Psoriasis
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Selected localized plaque-psoriasis and comorbidity principles from the official AAD guideline highlights; intertriginous sites and systemic treatment require different choices.

sources.title: Psoriasis clinical guideline
sources.organization: American Academy of Dermatology
sources.edition: Current joint AAD-NPF guideline highlights; date not stated on this page

sections.title: Treat the appropriate site
sections.text: Topical corticosteroids are recommended for plaque psoriasis outside intertriginous areas. Site, potency and duration affect the treatment plan.

sections.title: Consider steroid-sparing treatment
sections.text: Vitamin D analogues and other selected steroid-sparing topicals can contribute to management. Prolonged corticosteroid use requires supervision.

sections.title: Look beyond the skin
sections.text: Assess relevant comorbidities, including psoriatic arthritis and cardiometabolic and mental-health concerns; coordinate care when findings warrant it.

questions.stem: An adult has limited plaque psoriasis on the trunk without flexural involvement. Which listed treatment has guideline support for local therapy?
questions.explanation: Topical corticosteroids are recommended for nonintertriginous plaque psoriasis.

distractorExplanations.B: An antibiotic is not routine plaque treatment.
distractorExplanations.D: Donepezil is not psoriasis treatment.

questions.learningObjective: Select local treatment for plaque psoriasis

questions.stem: A patient with psoriasis reports new swollen joints and morning stiffness. What is the best next concern to assess?

choices.text: Only the color of the skin plaques
Whether topical potency alone explains every joint symptom
No concern because psoriasis affects skin only

questions.explanation: Psoriatic arthritis is an important psoriasis comorbidity to assess.

distractorExplanations.A: The joint symptoms warrant attention.
distractorExplanations.C: Topical adjustment alone omits the joint concern.
distractorExplanations.D: Psoriasis can involve comorbid joint disease.

questions.learningObjective: Recognize joint symptoms needing psoriatic-arthritis assessment

conditions.name: Cellulitis
conditions.specialty: Neurologic, mental health, musculoskeletal and skin
conditions.overview: Typical nonpurulent cellulitis in otherwise stable adults; purulent abscesses, necrotizing infection and special exposures require different pathways.

sources.title: Practice Guidelines for the Diagnosis and Management of Skin and Soft Tissue Infections: 2014 Update by the Infectious Diseases Society of America
sources.organization: Infectious Diseases Society of America
sources.locator: Section IV recommendations 3, 4 and 7; cellulitis evidence summary

sections.title: Cover the likely organism
sections.text: Typical mild nonpurulent cellulitis without systemic illness calls for streptococcal coverage. Oral cephalexin is one suitable option when appropriate.

sections.title: Base extension on response
sections.text: A five-day course is recommended for uncomplicated cellulitis that improves; extend therapy when improvement is insufficient.

sections.title: Reassess concerning presentations
sections.text: Deeper infection concern, severe compromise or failed outpatient care can warrant hospitalization. A purulent collection requires an abscess-specific assessment.

questions.stem: A stable immunocompetent adult has mild nonpurulent leg cellulitis without fever, systemic signs, penetrating trauma or MRSA risk factors. There is no drug allergy. Which listed oral option is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Cephalexin provides appropriate coverage for typical mild nonpurulent cellulitis.

distractorExplanations.A: This is an antiviral.
distractorExplanations.D: This is not cellulitis treatment.

questions.learningObjective: Select therapy for uncomplicated nonpurulent cellulitis

questions.stem: An uncomplicated cellulitis episode has clearly improved after five days of appropriate antibiotics. What duration principle matches IDSA?

choices.text: Continue until every skin discoloration disappears
Five days can suffice when improving; extend if response is inadequate
Stop after one dose regardless of response

questions.explanation: Five days is recommended, with extension for inadequate improvement.

distractorExplanations.A: This is not the routine duration.
distractorExplanations.B: Residual appearance alone does not define the stated rule.
distractorExplanations.D: Routine combination therapy is not required.
distractorExplanations.E: One dose is not the recommended course.

questions.learningObjective: Use response to guide cellulitis duration
